Tell me in about 200 words why people in India are switching to UPI, with a short list of 3 reasons
6:10 PM

People in India are switching to UPI because paying is as easy as scanning a code, and it costs almost nothing. What began as a bank-to-bank transfer idea is now the default way to pay, from a tea stall to a wedding hall to monthly rent.

Three reasons stand out:

Free and simple. Customers pay no fee, and most small shops pay none either. Even a chai seller can accept money with a printed QR code and no card machine.
Instant, across banks. Money moves in seconds, at any hour, between any two bank accounts, using just a phone number or UPI ID.
One app, many uses. The same app pays bills, splits dinner, recharges phones and sends money to family. Easy setup and many languages brought first-time users in small towns on board.

Trust helped too. Every payment needs a PIN, you get a message right away, and the same rules work in every app. Once a few shops nearby accepted UPI, everyone else followed, because carrying cash started to feel like the slow option.
